packs.title: Space, Art & Green
packs.promise: Explore Houston through spaceflight, museum discoveries and unexpected green spaces.

q.s: Separate a fossil observation from a story about it.
st: Choose one fossil display in the open paleontology hall.
Find a visible feature such as a joint, tooth shape or body outline and read the accompanying interpretation.
Write two lines: what you can see, and what the museum says that evidence helps explain.

q.s: Notice the choices that support an animal’s day.
st: Choose one open habitat along a comfortable visitor route.
Collect three observations about shelter, movement or feeding arrangements without approaching animals.
Use a zoo interpretation panel or official animal-care page to connect one observation with a stated care practice.

q.s: Sketch or describe the space a sculpture leaves open.
st: Find an open permitted path in the Cullen Sculpture Garden.
Choose a work and look at the empty space beside or within its outline without touching it.
Sketch that empty space or describe its shape in words, then add a sentence about how it changes your view of the work.

packs.title: Hermann Park, Room by Room
packs.promise: Discover gardens, performance spaces and the small journeys between them.

q.s: Arrange your notes as an ingredient list with one question left for later.
st: Follow the permitted path beside the edible planting area.
Find three labeled plants and record which part people use, only when the label identifies it.
Arrange your notes as an ingredient list with one question left for later.

q.s: Record how their poses differ, keeping any biographical statement tied to the labels.
st: Choose two sculptures from the open walkway.
Find the identifying names and one visual detail distinguishing each work.
Record how their poses differ, keeping any biographical statement tied to the labels.

q.s: Sketch or describe an object beside its reflection or shadow.
st: Find a dry place beside the pool.
Choose a tree or built feature and compare it with its reflection; if the surface is disturbed, use its shadow.
Make a two-panel sketch or paired written descriptions of the object and its reflection or shadow, noting one difference.
